rationale: A wins because it finds four clean, separate doors into the story: exams, capital allocation, pharmacy distribution, and the retail-vs-online spend claim. "Warby Parker says store shoppers spend more than online buyers. It will not say how much." is an awkward, reportable metric angle, even if that wording needs tightening. B has useful bones, but "LensCrafters, EssilorLuxottica, Pearle Vision" and "historically defensible, insurance-tied" smuggle in an industry thesis the update did not supply. That is how a decent angle becomes a callback where the founder gets asked for proof they do not have.
gaps_in_A: "It will not say how much" turns an omitted figure in the update into a company refusal. Safer wording: the update does not provide the spend differential.
"Warby Parker built its brand on skipping the middleman" leans on outside Warby history, not the supplied facts. It is probably true, but blind judging does not reward probably.
"That moves Warby Parker from a glasses retailer toward an eye-care provider" is a strong frame that needs the employment model, exam count, and revenue role before it leaves the strategy doc.
The set does not fully exploit the incumbent-optical-chain competitive angle; it nods at pressure on incumbents but keeps the strongest competitive protagonist offstage.
gaps_in_B: "LensCrafters, EssilorLuxottica, Pearle Vision, and the big-box optical chains" are imported targets. The update did not name competitors, market share, or incumbent vulnerability.
"the historically defensible, insurance-tied part of the optical business the incumbents have owned" is a whole market thesis wearing a borrowed suit. It needs evidence before it can carry an angle.
"A DTC eyewear brand is quietly becoming a place you get your eyes checked" overlaps hard with the first optometrist angle. Different altitude, same load-bearing fact.
"broader migration of basic health services into retail footprints" is a trend claim without the trend proof. B admits the hole, but then keeps the angle anyway. Pick a lane.
